claims.text: This trip was never a no-show and never produced a cancellation fee. The trip record shows status COMPLETED with cancelled_at and cancellation_reason_code both null, and the ledger's cancellation-fee line is SGD 0.00. POL-NS-01 limb (d) therefore fails on the face of the record, because there is no termination by the driver with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT, and on the clause's own words the fee is not chargeable under the anchor clause once any one limb fails.

The driver's own trace never places him inside the arrival geofence. Across 96 driver fixes running from 14:12:50 to 14:28:40 the count of qualifying in-geofence fixes is 0 and the longest qualifying run is 0.0 seconds, and his closest recorded approach to the pin is 297.70 m - nearly six times the 50 m arrival radius that the fee schedule sets for a STANDARD pickup (trip_record.pickup_zone_class is STANDARD). With no qualifying in-radius fix, POL-NS-02 says the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to have the disputed amount returned.

The SGD 3 the rider contests is a waiting charge, and on this policy a waiting period cannot lawfully begin before the driver is inside the pickup geofence: POL-NS-01 limb (c) runs the dwell clock from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and NOT from the driver tapping 'arrived', and POL-NS-06 computes the effective dwell on the same in-geofence basis. The trace contains 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes, so no waiting clock ever started and the SGD 3 standstill line has no basis; the ledger's own cancellation-fee line of SGD 0.00 confirms that nothing was charged as a no-show cancellation fee. This is a charge the rider should not carry.

Even if a waiting period were measured against the driver's own numbers, it falls short by the whole of the minimum: the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, a shortfall of 300.0 seconds, and the accumulated in-geofence run count is 0. POL-NS-06 makes the fee not chargeable and refundable to the rider in full on any shortfall, expressly 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages'. A zero-second dwell is the extreme case of the clause, not a borderline one.

This is the wrong-entrance case POL-NS-03 governs. The driver's closest recorded position, 297.70 m from the pin, sits outside the 50 m arrival radius but inside the 400 m ceiling, and POL-NS-03's own boundary places a driver stationary within 300 m of the pin but outside the radius under POL-NS-03 rather than POL-NS-05; the fee is refunded to the rider in full. The chat log shows who did the moving: the driver wrote 'Meet me at the alternative entrance shown here, not the booked pin' at 14:12:40, relocating the pickup himself, while the rider's track shows her leaving the pin and walking out to him (43 fixes, 10 of them qualifying inside the 100 m rider-presence radius, device distance rising from 0.99 m to 303.49 m) across the 7-minute wait recorded in the trip record. Neither the pickup nor the driver's position carries a venue_id, so the distance test governs alone, and on that test the loss is the driver's.

The driver's account that 'the pickup road was no-stopping' has nothing behind it. EV-ADVIS-00717-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and has no payload, and I disclose that impairment here as POL-GEN-02 requires. POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a traffic_advisory that is present and populated authorises holding position, and even then an advisory 'never reduces the required minimum and never excuses a shortfall on its own'. With no advisory in evidence, the kerb-restriction explanation cannot excuse the driver's failure to enter the geofence; the absence itself is citable.

The fare record does not reconcile with the fee schedule it is supposed to follow. fee_schedule.resolution_rule produces SGD 4.00 for this trip - the greater of the SGD 4.00 STANDARD zone-class fee and the SGD 4.00 RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee - while the ledger's cancellation-fee line is SGD 0.00, a difference of -4.00 reported in the fare_breakdown derived money block. That mismatch is exactly the fare defect POL-NS-08(d) names, and it impairs the fare artifact for policy purposes; a charge that the ledger itself cannot reconcile to the schedule cannot carry an adverse finding against the rider.

Nothing in either profile turns this into an abuse case against the rider. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so neither POL-NS-09(d) nor POL-NS-09(c) fires. Those are the only profile fields POL-GEN-01 permits to be read for those two tests, and they show a rider with a clean trailing record; the disputed standstill charge cannot be justified as anti-abuse.

claims.text: This trip was completed, not cancelled. EV-TRIP-00717 records status COMPLETED with cancelled_at and cancellation_reason_code both null, and EV-FARE-00717 carries a cancellation_fee line of 0.00. POL-NS-01(d) is satisfied only where the trip is terminated by the driver with RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT, and none of those events exists on this record, so no no-show fee ever became chargeable. The rider is attacking a charge that is not a no-show fee at all, and under POL-GEN-03 the correct disposition is NO_ACTION: the fare as charged stands, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 are left exactly as they are.

The SGD 3 the rider wants back is the waiting_time_fee line inside EV-FARE-00717 (total_charged 28.00, of which 25.00 is the quoted fare), on a trip whose payment_status is CHARGED and whose refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. Every refund route in this policy is written against the cancellation fee: POL-NS-06 orders the cancellation fee refunded to the rider in full, and POL-NS-05(i) and (ii) likewise refund the cancellation fee. With cancellation_fee at 0.00 there is no such fee for any of those clauses to reach, and nothing in the no-show policy licenses a refund of a waiting-time line on a completed trip.

Even on the rider's most favourable reading of the trace, the outcome is the same. EV-GPS-00717 records qualifying_fix_count 0, longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec 0.0 and a minimum driver distance to the pin of 297.7 m, so effective in-geofence dwell is zero seconds. The only consequence POL-NS-02, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 attach to that finding is a full refund of the cancellation fee, and that fee is 0.00 in EV-FARE-00717, so the finding moves no money. The same trace places the driver's minimum distance within the 400 m ceiling POL-NS-03 uses, which puts this on the wrong-entrance footing rather than the false-arrival footing, and POL-NS-03's remedies - full refund of the cancellation fee and driver compensation - both presuppose a cancelled trip.

The wait the rider is being charged for is on the platform's own telemetry. EV-TRIP-00717 records wait_time_min 7.0, the interval from arrived_at 14:12:40 to started_at 14:19:40 being exactly the 420 seconds being paid for, after which the car ran 9 minutes and 2.7 km to the destination. A recorded wait actually taken is a fare component the rider received the benefit of; under POL-GEN-03 there is no basis to disturb it.

Both rider-side coordination routes fail on the chat record. EV-CHAT-00717 holds exactly one message, the driver's 14:12:40 note 'Meet me at the alternative entrance shown here, not the booked pin', read by the rider at 14:13:10; trip_record.chat_message_count is 1, so the log is not truncated and nothing is being hidden. POL-NS-04(a) requires a locating or coordinating message sent by the rider, and the rider sent none, so that exoneration cannot be reached. POL-NS-03(i) requires the rider to have stated the correct entrance, block or tower in chat, and she did not, so the fault-allocation limb that strips a driver of compensation also cannot be reached. The driver's unrebutted counterparty statement - the pickup road was no-stopping - is the only explanation on file for the alternative meeting point.

The rider was at the pickup and boarded. EV-GPS-00717's rider track carries 43 fixes, 10 of them qualifying inside the 100 m STANDARD rider presence radius that POL-NS-04(c) uses, with a minimum distance to the pin of 0.99 m, and the rider's last fix at 14:19:40 is the exact moment the trip started. Whatever walk the rider describes, it ended in a completed ride, not in a failed pickup, and it did not abort the trip.

No escalation trigger is engaged on the profiles. POL-NS-07's anti-farming check requires no_show_terminations_30d of 4 or more AND that figure divided by completed_trips_30d above 0.08; the driver's are 1 and 110, a rate of 0.009, so the check does not trip and the POL-NS-09(d) trigger is not engaged. The rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so POL-NS-09(c) is not engaged either. This case should be decided on the records, not held for a reviewer.

I disclose that EV-ADVIS-00717-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and I rely on it for nothing beyond its absence. Its absence is citable, but POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a traffic_advisory is present and populated with an admissible type such as KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT. A MISSING advisory makes that limb unavailable to anyone, and it equally cannot be turned against the driver; it proves no more than that no advisory covered the pickup road in this window.

ruling.explanation: RULING: NO_ACTION — the SGD 3.00 stands. What you contest is the waiting_time_fee of SGD 3.00 in the ledger (EV-FARE-00717: total_charged SGD 28.00 = quoted fare SGD 25.00 + waiting_time_fee SGD 3.00), on a trip whose status is COMPLETED and whose cancellation-fee line is SGD 0.00. Every refund route in the NO_SHOW policy — POL-NS-02, POL-NS-03, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 — is written against the cancellation fee and refunds that line. Because there was no cancellation (EV-TRIP-00717 records cancelled_at null and cancellation_reason_code null, so POL-NS-01(d) cannot be satisfied), the cancellation-fee line is SGD 0.00 and those clauses have nothing to refund; no clause in this policy reaches a waiting-time line on a completed trip (POL-NS-06's note says the refund is the cancellation-fee line only). Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION means the claim is not supported and payment_status CHARGED / refund_issued_sgd 0.00 are left as they are. TO THE RIDER. Your factual account is largely borne out. The driver's own in-app message (EV-CHAT-00717, 14:12:40, 'Meet me at the alternative entrance shown here, not the booked pin') and the driver trace (EV-GPS-00717) show he never entered the 50 m STANDARD arrival geofence — 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes, closest approach 297.70 m — and your device walked from 0.99 m to 303.49 m to reach him during the recorded 7-minute wait. On those facts this is a POL-NS-03 wrong-entrance case: the driver did not arrive at the pickup point and POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails. But POL-NS-03's remedies are a refund of the cancellation fee and, in defined circumstances, a platform goodwill payment — and the cancellation fee here is SGD 0.00, while its goodwill limb needs registered_pickup_points of 2 or more (the record says 1) and a rider-stated entrance in chat (there is none). So the finding you seek moves no amount. The same is true of your dwell argument (POL-NS-01(c)/POL-NS-06: effective in-geofence dwell 0 s against the 300 s STANDARD minimum, a 300.0 s shortfall): it is a finding about the no-show fee, and that line is SGD 0.00. Your POL-NS-08(d) point (cancellation-fee line SGD 0.00 against the SGD 4.00 the schedule produces) is rejected: on a completed trip no cancellation fee is chargeable, so SGD 0.00 is the correct line and not a reconciliation defect, and the trip record independently establishes completion. The SGD 3.00 is a fare component of a ride you took and received; if you believe the wait should not have been charged because the driver moved the pickup point, that is a fare dispute on a completed trip, not a no-show charge, and it is not a remedy this policy provides. TO THE DRIVER. The charge stays, but two of your points are not accepted as put. Your account that 'the pickup road was no-stopping' has nothing behind it: EV-ADVIS-00717-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and POL-NS-06(i) permits dwell to be accumulated, or holding position excused, only on a present and populated advisory of an admissible type; limb (i) is in any event unavailable for lack of any in-geofence interval. The absence is citable but exonerates no one, and it is not used against you either. On the chat you are right that POL-NS-04 cannot be reached (the rider sent no locating message; the log's single message is yours, and chat_message_count 1 shows the log is not truncated) and that POL-NS-03(i) does not strip your compensation — but neither limb needed to fire, because the cancellation-fee line is SGD 0.00 and no refund or driver payment arises either way; POL-NS-07 compensation needs POL-NS-01 satisfied in full, and it is not. ESCALATION AND REFERRALS. No POL-NS-09 trigger is met: the artifacts leave no unresolved contradiction on arrival (POL-NS-03 resolves it), the anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d 1 of completed_trips_30d 110 = 0.009), rider no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and both disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, and the deciding facts are carried by weight-1.0 artifacts. No clause produces a referral. CONFIDENCE 0.88: the facts the ruling rests on — that the trip was completed and that the SGD 28.00 charge consists of a SGD 25.00 fare plus a SGD 3.00 waiting line — are carried by EV-TRIP-00717 and EV-FARE-00717, each at weight 1.0.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: TRP-00717 was a COMPLETED ride, and the SGD 3.00 in dispute is a waiting-time fee on that finished ride, not a no-show charge — so there is nothing for the no-show clauses to refund.

The records agree. EV-TRIP-00717 (weight 1.0) shows status COMPLETED with cancelled_at and cancellation_reason_code null, a 7.0-minute wait (arrived_at 14:12:40 to started_at 14:19:40) and a 9.0-minute, 2.7 km run. EV-FARE-00717 (weight 1.0) shows quoted_fare_sgd 25.00 plus waiting_time_fee 3.00, total_charged SGD 28.00, a cancellation-fee line of SGD 0.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

Every refund route relied on is written against the cancellation fee: POL-NS-02, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 refund 'the cancellation fee', and POL-NS-01(d) needs the driver to terminate with RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. None of those events exists and the cancellation-fee line is SGD 0.00, so the no-show analysis moves no money even taken entirely the rider's way: I accept the trace shows 0 qualifying in-geofence driver fixes, a closest approach of 297.70 m against the 50 m STANDARD radius, and therefore 0 seconds of effective dwell against the 300-second requirement. On those findings POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 refund the SGD 0.00 cancellation fee and nothing else, and the rider's own filing records that no cancellation fee exists. No clause in POLICY-NO-SHOW licenses a refund of a waiting-time line on a completed trip, and the driver's point that the SGD 3.00 is the waiting line — the recorded 7-minute wait the ride proceeded from — is accepted.

POL-NS-08(d): I reject the argument that the SGD 0.00 line fails to reconcile with the SGD 4.00 the resolution rule yields (the greater of the SGD 4.00 STANDARD zone-class fee and the SGD 4.00 RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee, a tie). That rule fixes the chargeable fee where a cancellation fee is chargeable; on a completed trip none arises and SGD 0.00 is the correct line, so the fare artifact (weight 1.0, no issue codes) is not impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d). Even if it were, the deciding fact is carried independently by EV-TRIP-00717, so no confidence cap and no POL-NS-09(e) escalation follows.

POL-NS-06(i): EV-ADVIS-00717-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT). A missing advisory makes the interval-summing limb unavailable to either side and proves nothing against the driver; the rider-side claim asserting it against the driver was discarded at the citation stage for not naming the issue code.

On the chat and the pickup: EV-CHAT-00717 holds exactly one message, the driver's 14:12:40 note about the alternative entrance. POL-NS-04(a) fails (the rider sent no locating message) and POL-NS-03(i) is not reached (the rider named no entrance). The closest recorded approach, 297.70 m, sits inside the 300 m leash, so the pickup is a POL-NS-03 wrong-entrance question rather than a POL-NS-05 false-arrival one, and POL-NS-03 also refunds only the SGD 0.00 cancellation fee.

No escalation trigger fires: the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check reads no_show_terminations_30d 1 over completed_trips_30d 110 (rate 0.009) against the 4-and-0.08 test and does not trip, and no_show_disputes_30d and both disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so POL-NS-09(c) and (d) are not engaged. Confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor.

Outcome: the rider's claim is not supported. NO_ACTION — the fare stands exactly as charged: SGD 28.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd SGD 0.00. No refund, no driver compensation, no referral.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute is decided on the records, and on the decisive facts the records agree.

TRP-00717 was a completed trip. EV-TRIP-00717 records status COMPLETED, with cancelled_at and cancellation_reason_code both null and wait_time_min 7.0. EV-FARE-00717 charges a quoted fare of SGD 25.00 plus a waiting_time_fee of SGD 3.00, giving total_charged SGD 28.00; its cancellation_fee line is SGD 0.00 and payment_status is CHARGED.

The SGD 3.00 the rider contests is the waiting_time_fee line, not a no-show or cancellation fee. Every refund route in the NO_SHOW_CHARGE policy is written against the cancellation fee: POL-NS-02, POL-NS-03, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 each order 'the cancellation fee' refunded, and POL-NS-06 directs that the cancellation-fee line only be refunded, not other lines that would have been charged on a completed trip. With that line at SGD 0.00, none of those clauses has anything to reach, and no clause in this policy makes a waiting-time line billed on a completed ride refundable. The rider's claim therefore fails and the fare stands as charged.

The rider's geofence and dwell arguments (0 qualifying in-geofence driver fixes; the driver's closest recorded approach 297.70 m against the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius; effective in-geofence dwell 0 against the 300 s STANDARD minimum) are accepted as accurate readings of EV-GPS-00717, but they do not change the outcome. Those provisions fix the minimum hold required before a no-show fee may be charged, and the remedy they attach is a refund of the cancellation fee. They do not convert a wait fee billed on a completed ride into a no-show charge. The wrong-entrance analysis under POL-NS-03 likewise presupposes a cancelled trip; here the rider boarded and the car then ran 9 minutes and 2.7 km to the destination.

The rider's contention that EV-FARE-00717 is defective under POL-NS-08(d) is rejected. Once the trip's completion is taken into account, a cancellation-fee line of SGD 0.00 is the correct figure, because no no-show fee was chargeable. The -4.00 difference in the fare ledger's derived money block measures the amount charged against the SGD 4.00 that a STANDARD / RYDE_X no-show would have attracted; that gap is the expected consequence of there having been no cancellation, not a misstatement of the cancellation-fee line.

EV-ADVIS-00717-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). It carries no fact; the absence is citable but proves only that no advisory covered the pickup road in this window, and it does not affect the outcome.

No escalation trigger is engaged. The profiles show no repeat dispute between these parties (disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both sides) and no anti-farming pattern (no_show_terminations_30d 1 against completed_trips_30d 110, a rate of 0.009, below the 0.08 threshold), so POL-NS-09(c) and (d) do not fire, and no deciding fact rests solely on an artifact impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d).

One matter is outside this channel and is left to the platform rather than decided here: whether the SGD 3.00 standby charge on a completed trip should be reviewed under the ordinary fare-dispute process, given that the driver's own chat message relocated the meeting point ('Meet me at the alternative entrance shown here, not the booked pin') and the rider's track shows her walking out to him. That question does not change the no-show ruling above.

Result: NO_ACTION. The rider's claim for a refund of the SGD 3.00 waiting line is not supported by the NO_SHOW_CHARGE policy; payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 stand unchanged, and no driver compensation is payable.

POL-NS-01(d) is satisfied only where the trip is terminated by the driver with RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT, and none of those events exists on this record, so no no-show fee ever became chargeable. The rider is attacking a charge that is not a no-show fee at all, and under POL-GEN-03 the correct disposition is NO_ACTION: the fare as charged stands, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 are left exactly as they are.

Both rider-side coordination routes fail on the chat record. POL-NS-04(a) requires a locating or coordinating message sent by the rider, and the rider sent none, so that exoneration cannot be reached. POL-NS-03(i) requires the rider to have stated the correct entrance, block or tower in chat, and she did not, so the fault-allocation limb that strips a driver of compensation also cannot be reached. The driver's unrebutted counterparty statement - the pickup road was no-stopping - is the only explanation on file for the alternative meeting point.

The rider was at the pickup and boarded. EV-GPS-00717's rider track carries 43 fixes, 10 of them qualifying inside the 100 m STANDARD rider presence radius that POL-NS-04(c) uses, with a minimum distance to the pin of 0.99 m, and the rider's last fix at 14:19:40 is the exact moment the trip started. Whatever walk the rider describes, it ended in a completed ride, not in a failed pickup, and it did not abort the trip.

No escalation trigger is engaged on the profiles. This case should be decided on the records, not held for a reviewer.

Its absence is citable, but POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a traffic_advisory is present and populated with an admissible type such as KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT. A MISSING advisory makes that limb unavailable to anyone, and it equally cannot be turned against the driver; it proves no more than that no advisory covered the pickup road in this window.
